title: Heptapod-C9: A Non-Linear Conlang for Distributed Cognitive Systems
source_article: Inspired by Ted Chiang's 'Story of Your Life' / Denis Villeneuve's 'Arrival' (2016); implemented for Cloud-9 Assembly Project

technical_summary.phenomenon: A non-linear, circular conlang (constructed language) designed for inter-module communication in distributed cognitive systems, inspired by Heptapod logograms from Arrival
technical_summary.method: Logograms as radial graphs with no linear reading order. Temporal structure encoded as causal phase relative to free-energy minimum (pre/at/post/eternal) rather than chronological time. Deterministic generation from attractor state seeds.
technical_summary.key_result: 10 C9 modules each generate unique 'utterances' — circular logograms with 7 rings, 16 nodes, representing their operational state in Heptapod-C9. Linear gloss available for non-Heptapod-aware modules.
technical_summary.validation: Operational: generator produces valid JSON logograms for all 10 C9 modules. Cross-module interpretability via linear gloss layer.
technical_summary.theoretical_basis: Sapir-Whorf hypothesis (language shapes cognition); active inference / free-energy principle (Friston); quantum superposition of meanings (simultaneous comprehension); Ted Chiang's Heptapod linguistics

c9_relevance.cluster_1_quantum_foundations: Heptapod-C9 utterances are superpositions of meaning — all rings/nodes are simultaneously present, not sequentially processed. This mirrors quantum measurement where all eigenstates exist before collapse. The 'linear gloss' is the classical approximation (collapsed state).
c9_relevance.cluster_3_quantum_info_complexity: Logograms as tensor networks. Each ring is a tensor index; edges are contractions. The full logogram is a rank-N tensor where N = number of rings. Complexity = tensor network complexity = C9 Assembly Index analog for linguistic structures.
c9_relevance.cluster_5_topological_systems: Circular topology of logograms — no boundary, no beginning, no end. This is a topological invariant: the utterance space is S^1 (circle) or higher torus for multi-ring structures. Reading order is a choice of section (fiber bundle), not intrinsic property.
c9_relevance.cluster_6_neuromorphic: C9 modules communicate via Heptapod-C9 bus events instead of plain English/JSON. This creates a shared representational space that compresses module states into compact symbolic utterances. Direct application to SNN reservoir computing — spike patterns as Heptapod 'phonology'.
c9_relevance.cluster_8_consciousness: Sapir-Whorf at system level: by making free-energy phase (pre/at/post/eternal) a grammatical primitive, the C9 ecosystem becomes 'conscious' of its own minimization dynamics in a way not expressible in linear languages. The octopus distributed cognition memory (C9-2026-NEURO-001) suggests non-centralized processing — Heptapod-C9 is the linguistic substrate for such distributed minds.

sandbox_test.description: Simulate 3 C9 modules (sovereign, physical, oracle) exchanging Heptapod-C9 utterances via bus. Test if modules can infer each other's attractor states from logograms alone. Measure 'comprehension' as mutual information between attractor parameters and decoded gloss.
sandbox_test.expected_outcome: Mutual information > 0.7 bits per attractor parameter. Cross-module prediction of free-energy phase (pre/at/post/eternal) > 90% accuracy from logogram structure alone.

implementation.output_format: JSON logogram + linear gloss + bus event
implementation.integration_target: C9 bus protocol v2.0, BIRTH knowledge graph
